item.title: “Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — eaten by crows, or by hawks, or by vultures, or by dogs,…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — eaten by crows, or by hawks, or by vultures, or by dogs, or by jackals, or by various worms. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: - “How, venerable sir, should one know, how should one see, so that ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises?” - “Monk, knowing and seeing…
item.description:
- “How, venerable sir, should one know, how should one see, so that ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises?” - “Monk, knowing and seeing the eye as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Knowing and seeing forms as impermanent … eye-consciousness … eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … knowing and seeing that feeling as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … Knowing and seeing the mind as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Phenomena … mind-consciousness … mind-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact … knowing and seeing that feeling as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Knowing thus, seeing thus, monks, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.53
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, it is because of not realizing, not penetrating the Four Noble Truths that you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course.…
item.description:
“Monks, it is because of not realizing, not penetrating the Four Noble Truths that you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course. What four? Because of not realizing, not penetrating the noble truth of suffering, monks, you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course … the noble truth of the origin of suffering … the noble truth of the cessation of suffering … Because of not realizing, not penetrating the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, monks, you and I have wandered and wandered through this long course. But now, monks, the noble truth of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the origin of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the cessation of suffering has been realized and penetrated. The noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been realized and penetrated. Cut off is craving for existence; destroyed is what leads to renewed existence. Now there is no further becoming.” The Blessed One said this … the Teacher further said:

From not seeing the four noble truths
As they really are,
One wanders for a long time
Through many births.
But when these are seen,
The root of rebirth is pulled out,
The root of suffering is cut off —
Now there is no further becoming.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 56.21
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monk, I say that there are these three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These three feelings have been spoken of by me. But,…
item.description:
“Monk, I say that there are these three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These three feelings have been spoken of by me. But, monk, I also say: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’ It is in relation to the impermanence of formations that this is said: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’ It is in relation to the nature of destruction, the nature of vanishing, the nature of fading away, the nature of cessation, the nature of change of formations that this is said: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 36.11
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, just as in the autumn, when the sky is clear and free of clouds, the sun, rising in the sky, dispels all darkness from…
item.description:
“Monks, just as in the autumn, when the sky is clear and free of clouds, the sun, rising in the sky, dispels all darkness from space, shines, glows, and blazes — so too, by developing and cultivating the perception of impermanence, all lust for sensual pleasures is abandoned, all lust for form is abandoned, all lust for existence is abandoned, all ignorance is abandoned, all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned. And how, monks, is the perception of impermanence developed and cultivated so that … all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned? ‘This is form, this is the arising of form, this is the cessation of form. This is feeling … this is perception … these are formations … this is consciousness, this is the arising of consciousness, this is the cessation of consciousness.’ It is when the perception of impermanence is developed and cultivated in this way, monks, that all lust for sensual pleasures is abandoned … all conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.102
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Like a pit of filth Accumulated for many years — So too, a defiled person Is very hard to cleanse. Monks, know such a person…
item.description:
“Like a pit of filth
Accumulated for many years —
So too, a defiled person
Is very hard to cleanse.

Monks, know such a person —
Attached to households,
With evil desires, evil intentions,
Evil conduct, evil practices.

All of you, being of one mind,
Should shun such a person.
Blow him away like dust,
Throw him out like rubbish.

Expel the verbose one,
The fake ascetic.
Having expelled evil desires,
Evil conduct, evil practices —

Keep yourselves pure,
Live with the pure,
Mindful, dwelling together,
Wise, and make an end of suffering.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 2.6
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Nun Upasanā: Upasanā, cross the strong flood, The flood so hard to cross, Subject to the King of Death. Bear this last body, Having…
item.description:
Elder Nun Upasanā:

Upasanā, cross the strong flood,
The flood so hard to cross,
Subject to the King of Death.
Bear this last body,
Having conquered Māra and his army.

From: Therīgāthā 1.10
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Greed gives rise to misfortune, Greed stirs up the mind. Greed is the inner fear Born within people. People do not recognize That special kind…
item.description:
“Greed gives rise to misfortune,
Greed stirs up the mind.
Greed is the inner fear
Born within people.
People do not recognize
That special kind of greed.

The greedy person knows not what is good,
The greedy person sees not the Dhamma.
Blindness and darkness occur
Where greed dwells together.

One who has abandoned greed,
Not greedy for what is to be craved,
For him greed falls away
Like a drop of water from a lotus leaf.

Hatred gives rise to misfortune,
Hatred stirs up the mind.
Hatred is the inner fear
Born within people.
People do not recognize
That special kind of hatred.

The hateful person knows not what is good,
The hateful person sees not the Dhamma.
Blindness and darkness occur
Where hatred dwells together.

One who has abandoned hatred,
Not hating what is hateful,
For him hatred falls away
Like a palm fruit cut from its stalk.

Delusion gives rise to misfortune,
Delusion stirs up the mind.
Delusion is the inner fear
Born within people.
People do not recognize
That special kind of delusion.

The deluded person knows not what is good,
The deluded person sees not the Dhamma.
Blindness and darkness occur
Where delusion dwells together.

One who has abandoned delusion,
Not deluded about what is delusive,
That one dispels all darkness
Like the rising sun.”

From: Itivuttaka 88
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no production of future renewed existence. When there is no future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.38
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, taking up shields and weapons, donning…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, taking up shields and weapons, donning quiver and bow, they charge into battle with freshly plastered ramparts, and arrows are hurled, swords are drawn. There they are pierced by arrows, struck by spears, drenched with boiling dung, crushed by stones, and their heads are cut off by swords. There they meet death or deadly suffering. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, a mass of suffering visible here and now, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta
📖 Read this sutta
